description: Use this when the person wants to start an eviction case and has given you its facts: the ground, where the case starts, the property, the parties and their own attestations. Creates a draft case in the person’s account. Nothing is submitted. Add its documents with evictions_add_case_document. Pass an `idempotencyKey` and reuse it if you repeat the call, so a retry never makes a second case. For a property manager, `landlordId` (from evictions_list_landlords) names the owner the case is for and adds its saved management agreement to the case. Do not use this to change a case that already exists (use evictions_update_case). The result is the case, with `state` and `nextAction` (who it is waiting on and for what). Next: evictions_validate_case. Needs the person’s account: sign-in or an API key.

amountOwedCents.description: The total the tenant owes now, in US cents (150000 is $1,500.00).

attestations.description: The person’s own statements about the case. Ask the person for each one; never fill them in yourself. On an update, send all of them again: this object replaces the one stored.

authority.description: The person owns the property or is authorized to act for the owner in this eviction.

caresCovered.description: Whether the property is covered by the federal CARES Act.

lateBeforeNoticeMonth.description: For nonpayment: whether the tenant was late or behind on rent before the month the notice was given. A Texas petition states it.

notDiscriminatory.description: The eviction is not based on who the tenant is, such as their race, religion, sex, national origin, disability or family status.

notRetaliatory.description: The eviction is not in response to the tenant making a complaint, reporting a problem to an authority, or using a legal right.

servicemember.description: Whether the tenant is on active military duty; `unknown` is an accepted answer.

subsidized.description: Whether the tenant lives in subsidized housing or receives rental assistance, such as a housing voucher.

entryPoint.description: Where the case starts: `notice` (a notice to the tenant comes first), or `filing` when a notice was already served (then give `priorNotice`). Cannot be changed later.

freeText.description: Anything else the attorney should know.

ground.description: Why the case is brought: nonpayment of rent, a lease violation, or holdover (the tenant stayed after the lease ended). Cannot be changed later.

idempotencyKey.description: Sent as the Idempotency-Key header (printable ASCII, no spaces): a repeat of the same request with the same key returns the first answer instead of a second case. Always pass one, and reuse it if you repeat the call.

landlordId.description: For a property manager: the id (lnd_...) of the landlord, the owner the case is for, from evictions_list_landlords. Its saved management agreement is added to the case as proof of authority. An archived landlord cannot be chosen, and a test-mode case cannot take one.

lease.description: The lease, when there is one.

endDate.description: The day the lease ends or ended, as YYYY-MM-DD.

monthToMonth.description: For a holdover in Texas: whether the tenancy is month to month.

monthlyRentCents.description: The monthly rent, in US cents (150000 is $1,500.00).

noticeMethods.description: In Georgia: the additional ways the rental agreement says a notice must be delivered, exactly as the lease states them, or the word `none`. The notice is posted on the door and states these methods too.

noticePeriodDays.description: In Texas: the notice period, in days, the written lease sets for this notice; 3 when the lease sets none.

startDate.description: The day the lease began, as YYYY-MM-DD.

terminationNoticeDate.description: For a month-to-month holdover in Texas: the day written notice ending the tenancy was given, as YYYY-MM-DD.

ledger.description: Rent charges and payments, for a nonpayment case.

amountCents.description: The amount, in US cents (150000 is $1,500.00).

date.description: The day of the charge or payment, as YYYY-MM-DD.

kind.description: For a charge only: what it is for. `other_fee` for any other charge; `eviction_fee`, `attorney_fee` or `court_cost` for a cost of the eviction itself, which no notice demands.

memo.description: What it was for, such as "October rent".

type.description: `charge` for rent or a fee owed, `payment` for money received.

parties.description: The plaintiff (the owner or manager) and each defendant (tenant).

isEntity.description: True when the party is a company rather than a person.

name.description: Full legal name of the person or company.

phone.description: The party’s telephone number, if known. A Texas petition states the tenant’s.

role.description: `plaintiff` for the owner or manager bringing the case, `defendant` for each tenant.

plaintiffContact.description: How the court reaches the plaintiff (owner or manager): a Texas petition states the address and telephone.

address.description: The plaintiff’s mailing address, on one line.

email.description: The plaintiff’s email address, if they want it on the filing.

priorNotice.description: The notice already served, for a case that starts at filing.

method.description: How it was served: handed to the tenant, left with another adult, posted on the door, or sent by certified or first-class mail.

periodDays.description: How many days the notice gave the tenant.

sealedEnvelope.description: In Georgia: whether the notice was posted in a sealed envelope on the door of the premises, as the person states it. The filing says so; a posted notice answered false there does not pass the prior-notice check.

servedDate.description: The day the notice was served, as YYYY-MM-DD.

type.description: Which notice it was, as written on it: a notice to vacate, a notice to pay rent or vacate, pay or quit, or cure or quit.

property.description: The rental property and its owner of record.

county.description: County, when known, as the US Census Bureau names it ("Henry County" or "Henry"); one the state does not have is refused.

line1.description: Street address of the rental property.

ownerOfRecord.description: The owner of the property as on the deed: a person or a company.

state.description: Two-letter state code, for example TX; DC for the District of Columbia. Test keys use the fictional state ZZ.

unit.description: Unit or apartment number, if any.

rentOwedCents.description: The unpaid rent alone, without late fees or other charges; 0 when no rent is owed. A court filing states it as the rent due, and rent claimed is never more, in US cents (150000 is $1,500.00).

date.description: The day it happened, as YYYY-MM-DD.

description.description: What the tenant did that breaks the lease, in the person’s words.

name: evictions_create_case
title: Create a draft case
